scope: Developer-only 120-cycle renderer return-idle CPU diagnostic on one Apple M4 Pro / macOS 27 host. Native sampled CPU identifies threshold crossings; renderer CDP profiles are correlational and cannot establish their cause or a release budget.
finding: Every captured threshold crossing is renderer-dominated in native process accounting. Each bracketed renderer V8 CPU profile spends 2.424–2.481 seconds of its approximately 2.53-second interval in V8 idle; its largest non-idle weights are 40.7–57.8 ms program and 7.5–52.8 ms garbage collection. This rules out a large sampled JavaScript stack within those flagged windows, but does not assign native renderer, compositor, PDF worker, GPU, operating-system scheduling, or unprofiled boundary work to a root cause.
decision: Keep the 10% return-idle threshold open. Do not relax it or change undo/PDF policy based on this correlational result. Next diagnostic work must observe renderer-native/GPU/worker activity or reproduce the event with a relevant controlled change.
limits: Fresh synthetic profile, not the seed run's live heap/history state.
Native libproc samples are periodic and CDP profiles only the renderer V8 isolate during the 2.5-second return-idle dwell.
No forced garbage collection, physical-device matrix, cold-cache control, or upper-bound attachment/image workload.
